terms.latin: aeger, aegrī m.; aegra, aegrae f.
evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.4: nē aegrī quidem omnēs convalēscunt (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 2.186: aegrō adhibēre medicīnam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The adjective aeger used as a noun; a doctor’s patients are aegrī.

sources: Lewis & Short: aeger
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 357.
